{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-pa-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"a9ad4f5758dee75ead83a3b6cc1a8d2b74952de880f55408182fcc030e8706ca","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-pa-class-c:lineage:42","source_registry_sha256":"643bc755bc144bbb64c82e5b21691c27918519b2f96f9b0ff96b63899c04fddb","source_liveness_sha256":"d125293461efac0b369397a252e58fe1686ca24cdc89a306e2ea205c1feddb7c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Intersections and curves","heading":"C — Intersections and curves","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Intersections and curves

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Intersection law specifies who must yield rather than granting an unconditional right to proceed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Even if another driver should yield, stop or yield as needed to prevent a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
At an unsignalized intersection, yield to crossing pedestrians whether or not a crosswalk is marked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk, even away from an intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
Yield when a pedestrian on a sidewalk crosses a driveway or alley. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
A turning driver must yield to pedestrians crossing with the light. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A01
Always yield to a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A01
Without contrary directions from traffic controls or police, a left-turning driver yields to oncoming traffic continuing straight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A01
A roundabout entrant yields to vehicles already circulating. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A01
Without other traffic-control directions, drivers arriving from different roads at about the same time yield to vehicles on their right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A01
From an alley, driveway or private road, wait for a clear public highway before entering. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A01
At a four-way stop, every vehicle stops and the earliest arrival should proceed first. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A01
At a four-way stop, simultaneous arrivals yield to the vehicle on the right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A01
Opposing vehicles at a four-way stop may proceed cautiously together while watching for turns. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A01
Read lane-assignment signs and markings early enough to choose the proper intersection lane in advance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A01
A driver mistakenly in a turn-only lane must make the marked turn rather than continue straight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A01
A driver wanting a turn but occupying a through-only lane must continue straight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A01
When adjacent lanes both permit left turns, remain in the selected lane during the turn because the neighboring driver may turn simultaneously. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A02
Cars parked on both sides facing one direction can be a clue that a street is one-way. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A02
A divided highway consists of opposing one-way roadways, usually separated by a physical barrier. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A02
For a right turn onto a divided highway, select a safe gap in traffic approaching from the left. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A02
For a left turn onto a divided highway, cross the first roadway through a safe gap from the left, then turn beyond the divider through a safe gap from the right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A02
Turning left before reaching the divider can put the vehicle into opposing traffic; heed WRONG WAY and DO NOT ENTER signs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A02
At a two-way stop, crossing a 30 mph road takes about a six-second gap in both directions, or about a clear block each way. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A02
Before a right turn, scan left, ahead, right and left again, allowing about eight seconds to a vehicle approaching from the left. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A02
Before a left turn, make sure oncoming traffic leaves a clear gap and cross-street traffic is stopped. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A02
Turning left from a minor road onto a major road calls for a nine-second gap to traffic approaching from the right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A02
Opposing left-turning drivers avoid tangling by turning before the center crossing point and entering the lane nearest the centerline. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A02
Do not begin a left turn until every lane to be crossed is visibly clear and the turn can be completed safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

Misconceptions: a legal priority never justifies a preventable crash; a wrong lane still dictates the marked maneuver; a roundabout entrant yields to circulating traffic.
Mnemonics: choose the lane early, find the gap, yield and scan the turn.
Glossary: jughandle routes a left turn through a right-side loop; a splitter island separates roundabout crossing stages; a hillcrest is a hill's top.
